clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old lifetime non-smoker presented with constitutional symptoms (fatigue, fever, night sweats) and respiratory symptoms (cough, pleuritic chest pain). Laboratory evaluation showed leukocytosis (13.5 WBC/μL) and viral panel was negative for RSV, influenza, and COVID-19. Imaging (CT/MRI) revealed a large heterogeneous mass extending from the right pulmonary hilum through the diaphragm, involving liver segments VII and VIII, with a small pleural effusion and no distant metastases. Percutaneous fine needle aspiration biopsy was performed and confirmed high-grade sarcomatoid carcinoma characterized by spindle cell proliferation with multinucleated giant cells and diffuse positivity for low molecular weight cytokeratin Cam 5.2, consistent with primary pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma. PET-CT staging showed no additional disease. Surgical consultation was obtained but surgery was deferred due to transdiaphragmatic invasion. The patient was initiated on platinum-based chemotherapy and tolerated treatment well at 3-week follow-up.
